evidence: Plin. NH 20.262: carduus flōrem purpureum mittit inter mediōs acūleōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The wild thistle; in Pliny also the garden kind eaten as a vegetable, the artichoke (cinara) (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: prō mollī violā, prō purpureō narcissō carduus et spīnīs surgit paliūrus acūtīs
phrases.english: in place of the soft violet, in place of the bright narcissus, the thistle comes up and the thorn with its sharp spines

phrases.latin: carduus flōrem purpureum mittit inter mediōs acūleōs
phrases.english: the thistle puts out a purple flower from among its prickles
